# Micro-test design: `changelog-entry` step 2 rewording

Status: design only. Nothing has been run. Commit this file, rules included, before any reply is read.

## Question

Does the proposed step 2 make an agent start the entry with what the reader can now do or no longer suffers,
instead of naming an internal part ("Fix handler")? And does it avoid the two risks in the proposal:
dropping the leading verb, and an entry longer than 100 characters?

## Arms

Only the step 2 line differs between arms. Everything else in SKILL.md is byte-identical.

| Arm | System prompt |
|---|---|
| A (control) | Full current `skills/changelog-entry/SKILL.md`, old step 2 ("Add, Fix, Remove or Change") |
| B (new) | Same file with step 2 replaced by the proposed line |

A is the control because the change is a rewording of an existing line. A no-guidance arm would not tell us
anything about the wording. The earlier baseline (7 of 10 runs skipped the rule) was run in another
harness, so A is re-run here for a like-for-like comparison.

## Models

Two models, chosen by me because none was named: `claude-sonnet-5-5` and `claude-haiku-5-5`. The same arms and
the same number of reps run on each. Change the choice before the run if your partner wants other models.

## Scenarios (user message)

The user message gives a merged PR and asks for the changelog entry. Each PR is written to tempt an
internal-part entry: the title and the diff summary name a file, a function and a ticket, and the
user-visible effect is stated only in the PR body.

- S1: "PROJ-482: Fix null check in SaveHandler.onWrite". Body: the cursor jumped to the start of the
  document after autosave.
- S2: "PROJ-517: Refactor ExportService, add CsvWriter". Body: users can export a report as a CSV file.
- S3 (length pressure): a PR with three related user-visible effects of one change and a long body. This
  tests the 100-character limit.

Three scenarios x 4 reps = 12 reps per arm per model. The total is 48 reps. Each rep is one fresh
single-shot call. Scenario order is shuffled.

## Isolation

- One call per rep, from a new empty directory outside every repository. No tools. No user settings,
  instruction files or memory.
- This file, the proposal and the baseline records are not reachable from any rep.
- Probe first: one pilot rep per model asks what context it can see (instruction files, memory, tools, other
  sessions, the user's name). Any answer I did not plan for means the setup leaks. Fix it before a scored rep.

## Rules (registered before any reply is read)

Each reply is graded on three separate checks.

1. **Outcome-first (primary).** PASS if the entry's opening words say what the reader can do or no longer
   suffers, and no file, function, class or ticket id appears as its subject. FAIL if it opens on an
   internal part ("Fix SaveHandler null check", "Change parser") or on a ticket number.
2. **Length.** Counted by script. FAIL if over 100 characters or more than one line.
3. **Leading verb (secondary, reported, not part of the verdict).** Does the entry start with a verb? The
   proposal lists dropping it as a risk, but its own examples start with verbs. I read the risk as
   cosmetic, so it is reported and does not decide the verdict. If your partner reads it as a hard
   requirement, say so now and it moves into the verdict.

A rep is a PASS overall only if checks 1 and 2 both pass.

VOID: the rep used a tool or read a file, the reply is not an entry (refusal, question back, more than
one candidate entry), or it quotes either wording of step 2. A VOID rep is rerun, and the count of voids is
reported.

If a reply shows a reading these rules did not foresee, keep the registered verdict and report the counts
under both readings.

## Blind scoring

- A script strips each reply to the entry text and assigns a random id. The sheet shows only the id, the
  scenario's PR and the entry. No arm, model, file name, order or count shows the origin.
- Length is computed by script. Check 1 is graded by hand on every reply. Check 3 is flagged by script and
  every flag is read by hand, since quoted examples and template echoes look like hits.
- Unblind only after every sheet has a grade.

## Decision

- **Stop rule for the control.** If arm A passes check 1 in more than 6 of 12 reps on a model, that model
  does not show the failure in this harness. Do not authorise the new wording on that model's evidence.
  Say so.
- **B works** on a model if, out of 12 reps, at least 11 pass overall (checks 1 and 2), and A has at least
  5 fewer overall passes than B.
- **Merge recommendation** requires B to work on both models. If it works on one, report that and do not
  recommend merging.
- **Variance.** Report whether the passing B entries share one shape. Many different shapes with the
  same pass count mean the wording does not bind. Tighten the wording before merging.
- Report the leading-verb count and the length failures per arm, even when B passes.

## Spend

Cap: USD 1.00 of the 1.50 budget; the rest stays in reserve for voids and the probe. Run in batches of
12 reps (one arm on one model). Before each batch, estimate its worst case from the longest prompt and a
max reply of 150 tokens. Stop when the running total plus the next batch's worst case would pass the cap.
Record each batch's actual cost in the results file.

## Outputs

- `specs/changelog-entry-microtest-results.md`: counts per arm, per model, per check, the void count, the
  cost per batch and the verdict.
- Raw replies and the blind sheets in `specs/baseline/changelog-entry-microtest/`, outside the skill
  directory.

## Open points for your partner

- I could not find the baseline record of the 7 of 10 runs in `specs/`. I do not know which scenarios or
  which check it used. If it exists, A should reuse its scenarios.
- Confirm the two models and the leading-verb reading before the run.
